title: Real numbers
note: ℕ conventions vary on whether 0 is included. ℤ = integers, ℚ = rational numbers.
wrong: x must be a positive integer.
x must be a rational number only.
x is a set of real numbers.

title: Absolute value
note: For a number, bars mean absolute value; for a set, bars count its elements.
wrong: Negative five has five set elements.
The square of negative five is five.
Negative five equals positive five.

title: Floor function
parts: Round 3.7 down to the greatest integer no larger than it
note: Floor rounds toward negative infinity, not simply toward zero.
wrong: Round 3.7 to the nearest integer, giving 3.
Round 3.7 up, giving 3.
Take the fractional part of 3.7, giving 3.

title: Ceiling function
parts: Round 3.2 up to the smallest integer no smaller than it
note: Ceiling is useful for the number of batches when a partial batch still counts.
wrong: Round 3.2 down to get 4.
Multiply 3.2 by itself to get 4.
Take the integer part of 3.2 to get 4.

title: Congruence modulo n
parts: a and b have the same remainder
note: Equivalently, n divides a − b. This appears in shift ciphers.
wrong: a and b must be exactly equal.
a divided by b equals n.
n is the remainder of a divided by b.

title: Divisibility
note: The divisor is on the left.
wrong: b divides a without remainder.
a is the quotient of b and 2.

title: Greatest common divisor
parts: The greatest positive integer dividing both a and b.
note: The greatest common divisor is no larger than either positive input.
wrong: The smallest positive multiple of both a and b.
The product of a and b.

title: Least common multiple
parts: The smallest positive integer that is a multiple of both a and b.
note: The least common multiple is the product only when positive inputs are coprime.
wrong: The largest integer dividing both inputs.
The smaller of a and b.

title: Prime valuation
parts: The exponent of the prime p in the factorisation of the positive integer n.
note: The subscript chooses the prime, while the result is an exponent.
wrong: The pth prime number after n.
The number of distinct prime factors of n.
